patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 4 removes the wheel-slip output port from WHEELS and the WHEELS-to-CONTROLLER signal interface. The retained controller slip-information input and response are consistent with claim 1, which specifies activation in response to detected slip but does not identify a signal source. The modeled housing, carrier, gear-set, clutch, chamber, pump, controller, bearings, and optional plenum/seal align with the cited claims/description.

functional_completeness.rationale: The model captures the claimed assembly elements and central sequence: pump delivery to the pressure chamber, selective clutch engagement, controller pump activation, and gear-set drive to wheels. Optional dependent-claim elements remain identified as optional. The unnamed slip-detection source is not guessed.

flow_consistency.rationale: The pump hydraulic output connects to chamber fluid input; controller command output connects to pump activation input; and gear-set rotational output connects to wheel input. The generic slip signal is retained only as a controller boundary input and is no longer attributed to WHEELS. The flow notes preserve the bearing-routed pathway without asserting a new pathway component.

claim_traceability.rationale: The cited passages support the modeled component roles and connections. Claim 1 supports the controller's response to detected slip, pump/chamber fluid communication, and gear-set drive to wheels; claims 2–3 support optional plenum and seal. The prior unsupported wheel-originating signal assertion has been removed.

interfaces.rationale: All represented subsystem interfaces connect existing compatible ports, are recorded once, and have matching flow types/directions. The previously problematic WHEELS slip port/interface is absent. The controller slip input remains unconnected, appropriately reflecting that the detection source is unspecified.

textbook_application.rationale: The model distinguishes internal interfaces and boundary interactions and uses typed signal, hydraulic, and mechanical flows. Textbook guidance supports this modeling approach only; patent facts remain grounded in patent passages.

summary: Revision 4 resolves the prior unsupported slip-source assumption: WHEELS has only its supported mechanical drive input, and no wheel-originating slip signal interface remains. The controller's generic detected-slip input is retained without a fabricated source. The hydraulic pump-to-chamber, controller-to-pump, and gear-set-to-wheels interfaces are compatible and consistently typed. Patent claims and cited description support the represented components and optional dependent-claim features. No unresolved material grounding, completeness, flow, traceability, interface, or textbook-application issue found.
